decision: Use OpenClaw as the personal messaging and agent runtime, not as the work-governance source of truth.
rationale: OpenClaw now covers runtime operations well, but DontPanic is stronger for plan-first implementation, audit, gates, and evidence. DontPanic was formerly named Jarvis; the legacy jarvis CLI alias may remain during migration.

decision: Archive the Axiom multi-tenant Cloudflare runtime for now instead of deleting it.
rationale: The tenant architecture is not needed for the personal setup, but it contains useful isolation and dashboard code that may be revived later.

decision: Use Discord as the shared collaboration app, Telegram as owner-private operations, and WhatsApp as optional notifications.
rationale: Discord has the best project/thread/channel model for deconflicting joint development. Telegram is better for private approvals. WhatsApp is less structured.

decision: Expose DontPanic to OpenClaw through a narrow wrapper, not arbitrary shell.
rationale: Most building happens on the laptop, so command blast radius matters more than multi-tenant isolation. Prefer the dontpanic command; keep jarvis only as a legacy alias fallback.

decision: Use canonical DontPanic paths and env vars for new OpenClaw, dashboard, and bridge work.
rationale: Commit 1db2464 introduced the future DontPanic shape: ~/.dontpanic/config.json, ~/.dontpanic/projects.json, per-project .dontpanic/dontpanic.json, DONTPANIC_* env vars, and the dontpanic_orchestrate module alias. Legacy ~/.jarvis, .jarvis/jarvis.json, JARVIS_* env vars, and the jarvis CLI alias remain compatibility fallbacks only.

decision: Reset F001/F002 to passes:false until local evidence is attached.
rationale: The untracked plan arrived with F001 and F002 marked passes:true but without verified_by or evidence_refs. The work may have happened externally, and INBOX.md plus openclaw-hardening.patch.json5 are preserved, but the local ledger does not yet contain enough feature-level evidence to support green flags. Keep the plan schema-valid and evidence-honest in main; a future close-out can flip the features back to passes:true when audit trails and evidence_refs are reattached.

decision: OpenClaw is the channel-agnostic notification router for DontPanic events. DontPanic emits a single NotifyEvent surface; OpenClaw fans out to Discord / Telegram / WhatsApp per policy.
rationale: Live dogfood (2026-05-09) of plan 2026-05-01-002 (Discord notification sink) raised two questions in sequence: should Discord become bidirectional inside DontPanic? AND is Discord even needed inside DontPanic when OpenClaw already integrates all three channels? Architectural answer per ECOSYSTEM.md / PRODUCT.md: NO to both. DontPanic is the verified software-delivery layer, NOT a personal-agent runtime; it does not own chat surfaces, mobile presence, interactions endpoints, OR per-channel knowledge (Telegram bot API / WhatsApp Business API / Discord webhook auth). OpenClaw absorbs ALL of those. The personal-axiom router (F006) ingests DontPanic NotifyEvents via either Path A (DontPanic webhook → local HTTP receiver in OpenClaw) or Path B (OpenClaw watches INBOX.md for new events). Path B is recommended — pull-based, port-free, survives restarts. DontPanic keeps its existing direct Discord sink as a public/solo-dev convenience; for the personal-axiom stack, the operator drops the direct ~/.dontpanic/discord.json and lets OpenClaw route. This absorbs both the bidirectional scope deferred in plan 2026-05-01-002 AND prevents DontPanic from ever needing per-channel sinks for Telegram/WhatsApp.
